meta.tolerance_rationale: Closed-form statistics in f64. describe uses std with ddof=1 and linear quantiles (numpy 'linear', pandas default); only summation order differs. The KDE is a sum of Gaussians evaluated on a linspace grid: exact up to exp/rounding. The pairplot sample uses pandas DataFrame.sample(random_state=42) (RandomState(42) without replacement): reproduce it or use the stored rows.

input.python_bug: Python concatenates X and y by index: this dataset's X index has gaps, so the app's preview/describe/pairplot show NaN rows and shifted labels. Do not reproduce.
input.kde_rules: seaborn 0.13 kdeplot defaults used by pairplot(diag_kind='kde'): gaussian_kde with Scott's factor n**(-1/5); kernel sd = factor * std(ddof=1); one KDE per hue level (common_grid=False): grid = linspace(min - 3*bw, max + 3*bw, 200) of that level; common_norm=True: density * n_level/n_total; levels with n < 2 or zero variance are skipped; fill=True.
input.hist_rules: histplot: bins = np.histogram_bin_edges(all values, 'auto') (common_bins=True), counts per hue level, multiple='layer'

correlation.method: pearson (DataFrame.corr); NaN where a column is constant
correlation.labels_rule: original X.columns (NOT the friendly names) + 'target' (class codes)
correlation.mask: np.triu(ones, k=0): upper triangle AND diagonal hidden
